targets.authors: Corbin, J. C., McElroy, T., & Black, C.
targets.title: Memory reﬂected in our decisions: Higher working memory capacity predicts greater bias in risky choice.
targets.evidence_quote: We replicated and extended Corbin et al.’s (2010) study to provide more robust evidence, and thus better inform theoretical accounts about the relationship between WMC and risky-choice framing.
targets.outcome_quote: Taken together, the present ﬁndings converge in casting doubt on the hypothesis of greater susceptibility to framing effects among individuals of higher WMC. All six preregistered tests, including three frequentist and three Bayesian ones, point in the same direction of no association.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Both close and extended replications are explicitly unsuccessful; all preregistered tests support no association, against the original positive association.

reasoning: Completed registered report with a new North American sample of 425; one original paper. Other theoretical, background, and task-material sources are not independent replication targets. Full 25-page article with references and appendices verified.
